question: Name the white precipitate formed in the reaction of sodium sulphate and barium chloride.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Barium sulphate**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Barium sulphate (BaSO₄) **is an **inorganic compound.**
 
• The white precipitate formed in the reaction between **sodium sulphate (Na₂SO₄) **and **barium chloride (BaCl₂)** is **barium sulphate (BaSO₄).**
 
• **Na₂​SO₄​+BaCl₂​ → BaSO₄​ (white precipitate)+2NaCl**
 
• **Barium sulphate (BaSO₄)** is **insoluble in water**, which causes it to form a white precipitate in this reaction.
 
• **Sodium chloride** (**NaCl) **remains in solution as it is **soluble in water.**
 
• Barium sulphate is used in** X-ray **imaging of the **digestive system** (barium meals or barium enemas), as it is **opaque to X-rays.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Barium hydroxide (Ba(OH)₂):
 
 
• **Ba(OH)₂ ​**​ **heatiⁿg**​ → **BaO+H₂​O.**
 
• **Barium hydroxide** Ba(OH)2 decomposes upon** heating **to form **barium oxide (**BaO) and** water (**H2​O)**. **
 
 
 
• Sodium chloride (NaCl):
 
 
• Sodium chloride, commonly known as** table salt **is a chemical compound with the formula **NaCl**.
 
• It's made up of **sodium (Na)** and **chlorine (Cl) **ions.
 
• When sodium chloride dissolves in water, it dissociates into its constituent ions.
 
• **NaCl****(s****)→****Na+****(a****q)****+Cl****−(****aq****). **
 
 
 
• Sodium oxide(Na₂O):
 
 
• **Sodium oxide** is a chemical compound with the formula **Na₂O**.
 
• It’s an ionic compound composed of **sodium (Na)** and **oxygen (O).**
 
• Sodium oxide is typically formed by the direct reaction of **sodium metal with oxygen.**
 
• **4Na(s)+O₂​(g)→2Na₂​O(s).**
